text:
cheng: Heads-up: I ran a long-run workload on staging and saw steady mem growth tied to KV slot churn + continuous-batch merges. Repro steps below.

maria: Ugh. Is this the same head-of-line stall we saw last quarter or something new?

cheng: Related but different. Last quarter was eviction thrash from bad watermarking. This one looks like slot attrition: lots of small fragments created when batches split mid-request, then the pager keeps pinning/reserving slots. pprof flamegraph points to kv_reclaim_loop + batch_merge_path.

sam: Can you paste the flamegraph/top callers?

cheng: Sure — snippet from pprof: 

```
pprof: top 10
50.2%  kv_reclaim_loop
18.7%  batch_merge_continuous
9.1%   kv_slot_alloc
6.3%   pager_lock_wait
3.8%   tensor_kernel_select
```

cheng: Also seeing a long tail in per-request latency when merges happen: 95p jumps from 45ms to 260ms every ~thousand requests. Memory delta: +820MB over 30k tokens for a single worker.

tara: Does kernel selection play into this? e.g., a fallback kernel that disables small-allocation fastpath and triggers fragmentation?

cheng: Maybe. On some sequences kernel-selector picks the 'fallback-quant' kernel for mid-length sequences which allocates slightly different KV layouts. When that happens concurrently with a batch split, the merge code does a conservative copy which pins old fragments until reclaim.

maria: Any quick repro? Worth triaging before offsite.

cheng: Repro steps: 
1) Start worker with continuous-batching enabled, batch_max=16, split_threshold=0.6
2) Drive synthetic traffic: 80% short (16 tokens), 20% long (4k tokens) with arrival jitter
3) After ~20m, watch `redis-kv-metrics` and `proc/mem` on worker

Commands I used: 
```
wrk -t4 -c200 -d1200s --lua=longtail.lua https://staging.infer
curl http://worker:9100/pprof/heap > heap.pb
```

sam: Good reproduction. Can you dump a kv-slot map snapshot? Also paste the pager logs around a stall.

cheng: Pager excerpt: 
```
[2024-04-18T03:12:45Z] pager: pinned slot=0x7f2a8c size=64 frag=3 ref=2
[2024-04-18T03:12:45Z] pager: reserve failed try=6 backoff=8ms
[2024-04-18T03:12:46Z] kv_reclaim: deferred reclaim N=124 waiting_for_batch_merge
[2024-04-18T03:12:46Z] batch_merge: split detected seq=4021 headlock=true
```

alex: Looks like headlock true lines coincide with long-tail latency. If a head batch holds the slot, subsequent small batches pile up — classic HOL blocking.

tara: Thoughts on mitigation? We could: 1) fast-path split without copying by using per-fragment refcounts; 2) make kernel selector prefer compatible layout for mixed workloads; 3) increase aggressive reclaim under low-util conditions.

maria: I like 1 + 2. 3 is sorta bandaid and might hurt throughput. Is per-fragment refcount expensive?

cheng: We profiled that: adding an atomic refcount increment/decrement adds ~0.8% CPU overhead in microbench but removes the copy in ~90% of split cases. Tradeoffs look good.

sam: Could we try an A/B: refcount on canary workers + bias kernel selection toward the 'stable-layout' for mixed seq distributions?

cheng: Yes, can deploy a canary with env KVS_REFCOUNT=1 and KERNEL_BIAS=stable. I'll run that tonight and post numbers.

devops-bot: deploy started: canary/kv-refcount-stable-20240418 by cheng. ETA 7m. :rocket:

cheng: Experiment results (after 6h): memory growth flattened, 95p latency dropped to 60ms, CPU up by 0.9%. KV fragmentation measured by "avg_fragments_per_slot" went from 2.7 -> 1.1.

tara: Nice! Any regression elsewhere (throughput, p50)?

cheng: p50 unchanged. Some micro-bumps in batch_merge latency (tail reduced). Kernel bias slightly increased cold-start latency for some short-only workloads but within SLOs.

maria: Great find. Next steps: 1) roll refcount into main branch behind feature flag, 2) add unit test for split-without-copy, 3) update kernel selector to consider mixed-workload heuristic, 4) monitor for regressions during traffic spike.

sam: I'll file an RFC and pair on unit tests. Assign to eng-runtime backlog?

cheng: Filed: https://redwood-internal/issue/ENGRT-9487 "KV fragment refcounts + kernel selector bias to reduce HOL during continuous batching". Assigning to eng-runtime.

maria: Thanks cheng and team. If the canary keeps stable, let's schedule a rollout next week. :thumbsup:
